data.summary:
Input: A 2D grid of characters and a list of strings.
Output: A list of all strings from the input list that can be formed by traversing adjacent cells in the grid.
Rules: Each cell can be used at most once per word. Words must be formed by moving to horizontally or vertically adjacent cells.
constraints: board and words consist of lowercase English letters

data.generator_code:
import random

def generate(rng, n):
    m = max(1, min(12, n))
    board = [[chr(rng.randint(ord('a'), ord('z'))) for _ in range(m)] for _ in range(m)]
    words = []
    for _ in range(min(n, 50)):
        length = rng.randint(1, 5)
        word = "".join(chr(rng.randint(ord('a'), ord('z'))) for _ in range(length))
        words.append(word)
    return [board, words]

def generate_worst(rng, n):
    m = 12
    board = [['a' for _ in range(m)] for _ in range(m)]
    words = ["a" * 10 for _ in range(min(n, 100))]
    return [board, words]

data.key_insight: Insert all words into a Trie (Prefix Tree) to efficiently search for multiple words simultaneously during a Depth-First Search (DFS) on the 2D grid, pruning branches that do not form valid prefixes.

steps.title: Build the Trie
steps.detail: Insert every word from the list into a Trie data structure, keeping track of the complete words at the leaf nodes.

steps.title: Iterate through the Grid
steps.detail: Start a DFS traversal from every cell in the 2D board if the cell's character exists in the root of the Trie.

steps.title: DFS with Backtracking
steps.detail: At each step, check if the current character is in the current Trie node. If a word is completed, add it to the result set and mark it to avoid duplicate additions. Temporarily mark the board cell as visited by modifying it, then restore it upon backtracking.

steps.title: Optimization (Pruning)
steps.detail: Remove leaf nodes from the Trie once their words are found to prevent redundant searches in future DFS steps.

data.space_complexity: O(sum of lengths of all words)

data.insight: Instead of searching for each word in the grid independently—which redundantly explores the same paths—we insert all words into a Trie. A single backtracking traversal across the grid can then match multiple words simultaneously by following valid prefixes down the Trie branches.

derivation.note: Loops over all words and their characters to build the Trie.
Recursively explores up to 4 directions for word length L from each starting cell.
Iterates over every cell in the M x n grid as a starting point.

data.time_summary: Building the Trie takes O(sum of word lengths). The DFS explores from every cell in the M x N grid, branching up to 4 ways for each of the L characters, resulting in O(M * N * 4^L) time combined with Trie prefix pruning.
data.space_summary: O(sum of lengths of all words) for storing the Trie nodes and children dictionaries, plus O(L) recursion stack space for the DFS.
data.takeaway: When searching for multiple string patterns in a grid or sequence, insert the patterns into a Trie to share common prefixes and avoid redundant searches.
mistakes: Forgetting to restore the board cell character after visiting it during backtracking.
Failing to prune empty Trie nodes after a word is matched, which leaves dead paths.
Checking words individually instead of matching prefixes concurrently via a Trie.

events.label: Coach: pattern, brute force and its bottleneck

data.pattern_summary: Trie and Backtracking combines a prefix tree with depth-first search to explore multiple search paths simultaneously and prune invalid branches early.

pattern_options.name: Trie and Backtracking
pattern_options.feedback: Correct. We store all target words in a Trie to check multiple words at once during our grid traversal and prune dead ends early.

pattern_options.name: Dynamic programming
pattern_options.feedback: Incorrect. The grid constraints and path dependency mean subproblems do not overlap in a way that allows simple table-based memoization.

pattern_options.name: Greedy search
pattern_options.feedback: Incorrect. Taking locally optimal moves on the grid will not guarantee finding valid complete words.

pattern_options.name: Two pointers
pattern_options.feedback: Incorrect. Two pointers applies to linear sequences, whereas this problem involves traversing a 2D grid in multiple directions.

signals.phrase: a list of all strings from the input list that can be formed
signals.hint: Searching for many different strings implies we want a structure that lets us look up multiple prefixes at once.

signals.phrase: by traversing adjacent cells in the grid
signals.hint: Moving cell by cell requires graph traversal like Depth-First Search.

data.brute_force_idea: For each word in the input list, perform a Depth-First Search from every matching starting cell in the 2D grid to see if the word can be spelled out.
data.brute_force_why: We loop through W words, and for each word we potentially search up to M * N starting positions, exploring up to 4 directions for each of the L characters in the word.
data.bottleneck: The provided code uses a Trie-like optimization structure conceptually, meaning the asymptotic complexity per word search is already bound by the traversal space rather than repeating independent word checks from scratch.
bottleneck_hints: Look at how many times we restart the grid search for separate words.
Notice that words starting with the same letters re-explore the exact same paths on the board.
Consider how a shared prefix tree could let you search for all words simultaneously in a single traversal.

data.overview: Word Search II finds all words from a list that can be constructed by sequentially adjacent cells in a 2D grid. It builds a Trie from the words and performs DFS starting from every cell in the grid, pruning paths that do not match any Trie prefix.
data.intuition: Imagine tracing a dictionary through a maze of letters. Instead of searching for one word at a time, you place your finger on the Trie root and explore all four directions simultaneously, dropping branches the moment the maze letters no longer match a valid prefix.

flow_nodes.label: Start Match?
flow_nodes.detail: Check if board[r][c] exists in the Trie root children.

flow_nodes.label: DFS Search
flow_nodes.detail: Explore adjacent cells recursively using backtracking.

flow_nodes.detail: Return the final list of found words.

pitfalls: Forgetting to restore the board cell character after backtracking (causes cells to remain permanently visited).
Failing to remove completed words or empty Trie nodes, leading to duplicate additions or TLE.
Not handling grid boundaries correctly during the 4-direction DFS traversal.
